datasource_item.source_question_text:
A Chinook salmon can jump out of water with a speed v0 and an angle 𝜃 above the horizontal. What is the speed of the fish when it is at the maximum height?
A. 𝑣0. [incorrect]
B. 𝑣0 cos𝜃. [correct]
C. 𝑣0 sin𝜃. [incorrect]
D. 0. [incorrect]
datasource_item.generated_question_text:

What is the speed of the ball when it is at the maximum height? (Neglect air
resistance.)
A. v0.
The speed is not generally the launch speed because the vertical component decreases to zero
at the top. [incorrect]
B. v0 cos θ.
At maximum height the vertical velocity is zero while the horizontal component remains v0 cos θ,
so the speed equals v0 cos θ. [correct]
C. v0 sin θ.
This is the initial vertical component, but at maximum height the vertical component is zero. [incorrect]
D. 0.
Only the vertical component becomes zero at the top; the horizontal component generally
remains nonzero. [incorrect]

|Favg| = |∆p|/∆t = 16.5/0.25 = 66 N. [correct]
B. 16.5 N.
This forgets to divide the impulse by the collision time to get average force. [incorrect]

This typically comes from doubling the correct force by mishandling the sign change or using
the wrong time interval. [incorrect]
D. None of the above is correct.
